subjects.name: Advanced Engineering Mathematics-I
subjects.gate_weightage: Very High - 13-15% of GATE ME paper (Engineering Mathematics compulsory)
subjects.rtu_priority: HIGH - Compulsory for 9+ CGPA, foundation for GATE
topics: Unit 1: Finite differences, operator relations, interpolation formulae (Newton's forward/backward, Gauss's, Stirling's), unequal intervals, divided difference, Lagrange's, numerical differentiation, numerical integration (Trapezoidal, Simpson's 1/3, 3/8)
Unit 2: ODE solutions (Taylor's series, Euler's, Modified Euler's, RK4, Milne's, Adams), polynomial/transcendental equations (Bisection, Newton-Raphson, Regula-Falsi)
Unit 3: Laplace Transform (definition, existence, properties, unit step, Dirac delta, Heaviside, periodic functions, inverse, convolution, integral evaluation, ODE solutions)
Unit 4: Fourier Transform (complex, sine, cosine transforms, properties, inverse, convolution, PDEs: 1D heat equation, 1D wave equation)
Unit 5: Z-Transform (definition, properties, convolution theorem, inverse, difference equations)

subjects.name: Engineering Mechanics
subjects.gate_weightage: High - ~7-10% of GATE ME paper, engineering mechanics fundamentals
subjects.rtu_priority: HIGH - Core subject for 9+ CGPA, strong overlap with GATE ME statics/dynamics
topics: Unit 1: Statics of particles/rigid bodies (fundamental laws, transmissibility, resultants/resolution, moments/couples, Varignon's theorem, force resolution, free-body diagrams, equilibrium, Lami's theorem); Plane trusses (types/support conditions/loading/determinacy/basic assumptions/method of joints/method of sections); Virtual work (principle, active-force diagrams, stability of equilibrium)

Unit 2: Centroid, Moment of Inertia, and Lifting Machines (centroid/CG, moment of inertia, parallel-axis theorem, perpendicular-axis theorem, radius of gyration, composite sections, polar moment, solid bodies); Lifting machines (MA/VR/efficiency/ideal machine/reversibility/law of machine/pulley systems/wheel/axle/Weston's block/worm/wheel/winch crabs/screw jack/differential screw jack)

Unit 3: Friction and Belt/Rope Drives (friction: types/laws/angle of friction/angle of repose/ladder friction/wedge friction/belt friction); Belt/rope drives: types/velocity ratio/slip effect/crowning/belt length/flat-belt tensions/power transmission/V-belt vs flat belt advantages/disadvantages)

Unit 4: Kinematics and Kinetics (particles/rigid bodies: velocity/acceleration/types of motion/equations/rectangular components/angular velocity/acceleration/radial/transverse/projectile motion on horizontal/inclined planes/relative motion); kinetics: Newton's second law/rectangular coordinates/radial/transverse components/rigid bodies in plane/D'Alembert's principle)

Unit 5: Work, Energy, Power, Impulse, and Momentum (work/energy/power: force/weight/spring force/couple/power/efficiency/energy/KE of rigid body/work-energy principle/conservative/non-conservative forces/conservation of energy); impulse/momentum: linear/angular momentum/impulse/momentum principles/linear impulse-momentum/angular momentum/impulse/conservation of angular momentum/rigid bodies angular momentum/central impact/oblique impact/variable mass systems/rockets

subjects.name: Mechanics of Solids
subjects.gate_weightage: Very High - ~13-15% of GATE ME paper, core subject alongside SOM
subjects.rtu_priority: HIGH - Core for 9+ CGPA, very strong RTU-GATE overlap (stress analysis, torsion, bending, columns), study alongside Thermodynamics and Maths
topics: Unit 1: Stress and Strain (elementary definitions/stress-strain relationships/elastic/plastic/viscoelastic behavior/tensile/compressive/shear/stress-strain curves/Hooke's law/Poisson's ratio/elastic constants for isotropic Hookean/anisotropic/orthotropic/tensile/compressive/shear stress/strain/thermal stresses/composite bars/static equilibrium equations/free-body diagrams/strain energy due to axial loading)

Unit 2: Members Subjected to Flexural Loads (simple bending theory/bending-moment diagrams/shear-force diagrams for different loading/support conditions/bending stresses/section modulus/transverse shear-stress distribution: circular/hollow circular/I-box/T/Angle sections/strain energy due to bending)

Unit 3: Principal Planes, Stresses, Strains, and Elastic Failure (principal stresses/strains under combined axial/bending/torsional loads/max normal/shear stresses/equivalent bending/twisting moment/Mohr's circle of stress/strain; theories of elastic failure: need/different theories/significance/comparison/applications)

Unit 4: Torsion and Stability of Equilibrium (torsional shear stress:solid/hollow/stepped circular shafts/angular deflection/power transmission/strain energy; stability: instability/elastic stability/long/short columns/ideal struts/Euler's crippling-load formula for different end conditions/equivalent length/eccentric loading/Rankine formula/other empirical relations)

Unit 5: Beam Deflection and Thin-Walled Pressure Vessels (relations between deflection/BM/SF/load/beam/shaft deflection under static loading: area-moment method/direct-integration method; thin-walled pressure vessels: cylindrical vessel stresses/spherical vessel stresses)

10. Bending tests and Young's modulus determination through beam deflection
11. Creep testing using creep-testing machine
